{
  "hypothesis": "Predicted that the intervention group would shoot faster than the control group in correctly detected shoot scenarios.",
  "design": "mixed, 2 (group: intervention vs. control) x 2 (measurement time: pre-test vs. post-test)",
  "manipulation_or_predictor": "An individual video-based firearms training intervention based on the Four-Component Instructional Design Model (4C/ID), focusing on situational awareness, tactical gaze control, and visual attention, compared to an active control training resembling traditional police firearms training.",
  "outcome_measure": "Response time (in milliseconds) between the detection of the black handgun and the participant's initial motor response (shot taken on the paper canvas) in correctly detected shoot scenarios.",
  "population_and_setting": "45 senior police officers recruited from the German Police University, tested in an indoor firing range lab setting.",
  "sample_size_total": 45,
  "recruitment_and_incentive": "Recruited via notices on campus; participation was voluntary; debriefed at the end of the study.",
  "analysis_plan": "Repeated measures ANOVA with the within-subject factor Time and the between-subject factor Group.",
  "preregistered_or_confirmatory": "preregistered",
  "other_methods_notes": "Participants used a gas-operated replica of a Heckler and Koch SFP9 handgun. Eye-tracking glasses were worn during testing. The intervention training included an 18-minute educational video and practical exercises; the control training included a 12-minute educational video and practical exercises. Seven participants were excluded from the response time analysis due to false negative decisions."
